title: Anchor First, Accelerate Next: Revolutionizing GNNs with PIM by Harnessing Stationary Data
problem: Graph neural network processing on PIM architectures suffers from cross-bank data movement; only 35.6% of data stays stationary within PIM units on average, degrading efficiency as PIM density increases.
motivation: PIM architectures promise near-memory computation, but irregular graph topologies and multi-bank layouts prevent effective data locality exploitation in GNN workloads.
method: Anchor architecture uses hardware-software co-design. Software-level Mastav graph partitioning algorithm allocates vertices and edges to maximize stationary data within PIM banks. Hardware-level customized dataflow ensures non-stationary data is accessed and distributed exactly once. An optimized communication mechanism reduces redundant transfers through critical path analysis.
key_novelty: First PIM architecture maximizing stationary data exploitation for GNNs through locality-preserving graph partitioning (Mastav) and single-pass non-stationary dataflow.
contributions: Mastav graph partitioning algorithm maximizing vertex/edge locality within PIM banks
Customized dataflow ensuring single-pass access to non-stationary data
Optimized communication reducing redundant transfers via critical path analysis
Significant latency and data movement reduction vs. prior schemes
primary_theme: Stationary-data-aware PIM for GNNs via locality-preserving partitioning
